First, notice that

$$
{[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we have been given the following diagonalization of $B:$

$$
B={{[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}\sqrt[60]{2} & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt[40]{2}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{{[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

Since $B=PD{P}^{-1}$, we can compute ${B}^{k}$ by using the formula 

$$
{B}^{k}=P{D}^{k}{P}^{-1}.
$$

Carrying out the necessary multiplication, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{120} & =P{D}^{120}{P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}\sqrt[60]{2} & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt[40]{2}\end{aligned}]}^{120}[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}(\sqrt[60]{2})^{120} & 0 \\ 0 & (\sqrt[40]{2})^{120}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{3}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & -24 \\ 12 & 32\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}40 & 24 \\ -48 & -28\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
